title: PKM lead 1: F4 solving degree of the Kummer tower at m = 3, N = 21 and m = 4, N = 20
status_note: Rescoped 2026-10-16 (claim audit): the m = 4, N = 20 cell is already answered, NEGATIVE: msolve 0.6.5 completed three productive degree-8 F4 rounds on both targets before its 5 GB cap, so D >= 8 at m = 4, N = 20 (research/ic_next10_20261014/03-pkm-degree/README.md; caveat: msolve on the raw presentation, f4_fp_tower not run there). The card's own rule reads that as strong evidence against boundedness at m = 4. Only the m = 3, N = 21 cell remains (inconclusive there: D >= 7, stopped by the wall before any degree-8 round). Blocked on hardware: the projection needs 133-146 GB (m = 3) of RAM against about 14 GB here, or a disk-backed B' reducer that is not built. The engine is pinned at the head of the open PR #1893. The engine has no checkpoint, so a run cannot resume; that must change, or the protocol must accept unresumable runs, before the card is ready.

question: Does the Kummer tower's F4 solving degree D stay at 7 at m = 3, N = 21 (extending the plateau from N = 15 to L = 6 levels), or does it rise? (The m = 4, N = 20 cell is answered: D >= 8.)
decision_value: The m = 4 half of this question is answered negatively (D >= 8 at m = 4, N = 20, research/ic_next10_20261014/03-pkm-degree/README.md), and m >= 4 is the only regime where a tower base can beat rho's exponent (RESEARCH_PKM_TOWER_ORACLE.md §3.7: m = 3 at best ties it). A rise to D = 8 at m = 3, N = 21 would extend the negative to m = 3; a plateau there does not by itself establish H1a under rule A1 (that needs L > 10, i.e. N >= 27 at m = 3) and, since m = 3 cannot beat rho's exponent, would at most justify the larger runs as a mechanism study.

resources.notes: Derived (research/pkm_dickson_torus_20261015/README.md §5, not run): m = 3, N = 21: 133-146 GB, 2.5-7.4e15 multiply-adds, 86-138 h single-threaded at the round-7 rate. Too low if D rises 7 -> 8. The m = 4, N = 20 cell (243-384 GB, 168-327 h) is dropped: answered by 03-pkm-degree. The round-6 full-rank exit cuts time to about 0.61x and leaves memory unchanged. The kernel is rayon-parallel, so a many-core node shortens wall time roughly by core count.

params.argv_note: Flags follow research/pkm_dickson_torus_20261015/run.sh (p1 = 15*2^27 + 1, the prime of the recorded Kummer rows the projection extrapolates). The --budget and --max-nnz caps, and whether one or two targets per cell, are fixed in PROTOCOL.md.

outputs.result_schema: pkm_tower_pilot JSONL rows (one per (m, N, target): D, width, steps, multiply-adds, peak memory)

cairn.notes: Two single heavy runs: claim one task per cell, run it with `cairn lab exec` (receipt + rows published together), re-claim before the TTL lapses as the heartbeat, release completed or failed. Not preemptible: the engine cannot checkpoint, so a preempted run loses its work.
